slides_data.notes: Hi there! This is a quick byte on functions.

☑️ Do This: Introduce the Painter as the object students will be controlling in their code. Emphasize that the Painter already has built-in abilities – move, turn, and paint. Students won't define how these actions work; instead, they'll learn how to tell the Painter what to do and when.
☑️ Do This: Explain that when students write alice = Painter(), they are creating a new Painter object and giving it a name (alice) so they can control it.
Painter() tells Python to create a new object using the Painter blueprint
"alice =" gives that new object a name so we can refer to it in our code.
🎙️ Say: A class is like a set of instructions or a blueprint. It doesn't do anything on its own, but it tells Python how to create something – like a Painter – that can do specific tasks.
🎙️ Say: Once you've created a Painter, it becomes an object. That object has things it knows – like where it is – and things it can do – like move or paint.

☑️ Do This: Click through the animated slide to explain that they can create multiple Painter objects. They both come from the same class (blueprint), but they are completely independent from one another. Be sure to clarify that alice and bob each have their own position, direction, and paint amount. We can give them different instructions, and they won't affect each other.

Teaching Tip
Students may assume that calling Painter() twice creates the same object reused. Reinforce that each call to Painter() creates a new object with its own state.

scenes.comment: Defining what an object is and its properties (attributes and methods).

scenes.comment: Explaining how to create multiple independent Painter objects.
scenes.speech: You can create multiple Painter objects. This new object, 'alice', has everything a Painter knows how to do: move, turn, paint. But it's its own object! If you later create another painter called 'bob', 'bob' and 'alice' are completely separate Painters. They can have different positions, directions, and even different amounts of paint.
